parts.note: a sense that sticks to the exact letters or words, as opposed to a figurative one; also an adjective for things relating to letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what some letters are meant to signify.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict, word-for-word reading is the one taken at face value, and the word also describes anything concerning alphabet characters.

parts.note: least means smallest, most modest in size
ways are manners or habits

explanation.surface: Describing the humblest behaviour, at any rate.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means 'at least' or 'in any case', a dialect or American way of saying anyway.

clue.text: Article includes a direction that is unbending

indicators.note: the word for an article holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a thing is an article or object
W, west, is a direction

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece containing an instruction that is rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unbending' suggests rigid; here it means relaxing, losing stiffness, as frost melts or a person warms up. 'Article' is not A or THE but a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Melting or becoming friendlier both mean losing stiffness, so a person relaxing their reserve is no longer stiff.

clue.text: Turned up in odd oriental trousers

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E, east, stands for oriental

explanation.surface: Turn-ups on a pair of strange Eastern trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' suggests trouser turn-ups; it describes a nose tilted upward at the tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub nose tilted upward at the tip is described with this French-derived adjective.

definitions.meaning: lugworms, burrowing marine worms used as fishing bait

explanation.surface: Earthworms that have ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Lugworms are dug as bait, and the same word is slang for ears or carrying-handles.

clue.text: One hundred antelope seen in the N Atlantic

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A hundred antelopes improbably spotted out in the North Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is an island nation that is found in the North Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is an island lying in the northern Atlantic Ocean, just below the Arctic Circle.

parts.note: in means fashionable
to haunt a place is to visit it often

explanation.surface: A trendy hangout that is exclusive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare happens seldom, not often.

clue.text: He's to change, showing characteristic spirit

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are made to change places

explanation.surface: A man's need to change reveals his true nature.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive character or guiding beliefs of a community or person are its spirit.

clue.text: Take steps to suit the music

definitions.meaning: to adapt a piece for different instruments or voices

explanation.surface: Taking action to make the music fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To organise plans, and to adapt a composition for other instruments, are two senses of the same verb.

indicators.note: the note is placed inside the word for father

parts.note: pop is father, as is dad
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A dreadful note in a pop song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like pop music; it means father.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means terrible, inspiring awe or fear.

parts.note: vast means very large

explanation.surface: Someone ordering a huge halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a nautical command, used by sailors to call 'stop!' or 'hold fast'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's interjection ordering someone to cease what they are doing.

clue.text: The wrong subject for an oral exam

definitions.text: The wrong subject for an oral exam

parts.words: The wrong subject for an oral exam
parts.note: the proverb says never look a present animal in the mouth (checking its teeth for age), so examining its mouth is the thing not to do

explanation.surface: A student revising the wrong topic before a spoken test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral exam' suggests a university viva; it means inspecting a mouth, as horse-dealers checked teeth to judge age.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying warns against inspecting the teeth of an animal you were given free, so it should never undergo a mouth inspection.

clue.text: With eight others, a man to suit us

definitions.text: With eight others, a man to suit us

parts.words: With eight others, a man to suit us
parts.note: the counting rhyme 'tinker, soldier, sailor, rich man, poor man, beggarman, thief' lists nine trades; one of them is the man who makes suits

explanation.surface: A man in a group of nine who is chosen to please us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit us' looks like 'satisfy us', but it means make suits for us; the nine are the trades in the British fortune-telling rhyme 'Tinker, Tailor', counted on cherry stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment-maker is one of the nine figures in the cherry-stone rhyme, and his trade is cutting suits.

indicators.note: the word for offspring takes in the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: seed can mean offspring or descendants, as in biblical usage
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Describing a family's children, with one boy among them as a veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hardened by long practice, like timber dried over time, is well versed.

clue.text: As hard as Princess Ida's castle

definitions.text: As hard as Princess Ida's castle

parts.words: As hard as Princess Ida's castle
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's opera Princess Ida the heroine's women's college is at Castle Adamant, adamant being a legendary unbreakable stone

explanation.surface: A comparison with the stronghold in a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; its castle is Castle Adamant, and the answer is the adjective from that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means unbreakably hard, like the mythical stone, from which the opera's castle takes its name.

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth a hundred-eyed giant set to watch over Io, hence a watchful protector
a newspaper title used by several papers, e.g. in Melbourne and Brighton

explanation.surface: Naming one newspaper, the Guardian, alongside a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like the British newspaper; it is the watchman of Greek myth, while the second sense really is a newspaper name.
explanation.definitionFit: The hundred-eyed watchman of myth gave his name to vigilant guards and to several newspaper titles.

definitions.meaning: an adverb meaning very probably, without question
read as two words, to be less uncertain, i.e. to question things to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is likely to feel more confident.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means 'surely, probably', and split in two it describes being less sceptical, i.e. more confident.

parts.note: a legal document proving ownership of property, the evidence of a right, which may be a transfer of land

explanation.surface: A sign pointing out the correct vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveyance' suggests a vehicle and 'right' a direction; in law conveyance is transfer of property and the right is ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal document evidencing ownership of land shows a right, and a conveyance is such a deed.

indicators.note: the word for stairs follows the word for the team

parts.note: a side is a team, such as a cricket or football eleven
steps are stairs

explanation.surface: Someone shunning the staircase late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After eleven' reads as a time; eleven is a team of eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge an issue or a blow is to evade it by moving aside.

parts.note: the blank in Dryden's portrait of Zimri in Absalom and Achitophel, a man who was everything by turns, including a political leader

explanation.surface: A line of verse listing a fickle man's many careers, with one gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash marks a missing word in Dryden's satirical line on Zimri (the Duke of Buckingham): 'Was chymist, fiddler, ___, and buffoon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dryden's line on Zimri lists the roles of a man who was by turns scientist, musician, politician and clown.

indicators.note: the sailor goes together with the word for solitary

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
alone means solitary

explanation.surface: A lonely sailor with a shellfish for company.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea snail called ormer or paua is an edible gastropod prized for its mother-of-pearl shell.

parts.note: taken as written
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: Something delivered to one particular man.
explanation.definitionFit: To lug or haul something about is to have carried it.

parts.note: a tin is a can
to foil is to frustrate or thwart

explanation.surface: Packaging that can be maddening to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb; it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheet used to wrap food is a kitchen packaging material.

clue.text: In a panic, father's beginning drinking

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word for a parent is used here

parts.note: lapping is drinking with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Dad, panicking, starts reaching for the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' looks like 'starting to', but it picks the first letter of 'father's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agitated or flustered, like a bird beating its wings, is the informal sense of being in a state.

explanation.surface: Someone getting cross at a fit of the vapours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The vapours' suggests an old-fashioned fit of hysteria; here it is smoke or gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Seething with rage and giving off smoky gas share one word.

indicators.note: the word for a job holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a post is a job
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Taking it that the position involves a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward something as a premise is to suppose it.

indicators.note: to sort letters is to rearrange them, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Describing the best kind of pretences.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceptive moves or shows of attacking are false pretences, a boxer's or fencer's dummy blows.

clue.text: Put up with the result of friction

explanation.surface: Tolerating the consequences of a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friction' suggests ill feeling; here it is physical rubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is informally to stand for it, and erosion from use is also called by this word.

definitions.meaning: illicitly distilled spirit, made without paying excise duty

explanation.surface: A dreamer's scheme involving tax-free alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty-free' suggests an airport shop; here it means bootleg liquor on which no tax is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both foolish fancy, like light from the night sky, and illicit spirit distilled by night.

clue.text: Draw forth approval in' a woman

indicators.note: the approval goes inside the woman's name

parts.note: Eve, the first woman
OK means approval or assent

explanation.surface: Coaxing approval out of a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To call up a memory or feeling is to summon or bring it out.

clue.text: Point to tiny haberdashery item — some confection

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
wee means tiny (Scottish and informal British)
a tie is sold in a gentlemen's outfitters

explanation.surface: Gesturing at a small item in a draper's shop, perhaps a frilly creation.
explanation.walkthrough: A haberdasher in Britain sells sewing goods, in America men's clothing; 'Point' looks like a verb but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugary sweet or candy is a piece of confectionery.

explanation.surface: Someone sorting through the questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse sieve gives the verb for sifting, and puzzling conundrums are also known by the same word.
